title: Connection pool drain + KV compaction caused tenant-facing 5xx waves; contain retries and patch eviction path
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Summary: Multiple customers reported intermittent 5xx errors and timeouts on the Hosted API between 2026-03-08 and 2026-03-10. Initial triage ruled out a single model variant or region. Investigation shows a compound failure: (1) the edge proxy connection pool experienced a slow-drain condition under tenant burst, leading to sporadic connection resets, (2) a background KV cache compaction sweep was performing a full shard scan during high QPS which caused tail latency spikes and transient cache corruption, and (3) aggressive client retry patterns amplified load and caused cascading backend overloads. This ticket contains the immediate containment steps, the hotfix to the eviction/compaction path, SDK retry guidance, rollout plan, and follow-ups for long-term resilience.
reproduction_steps: Simulate tenant burst: 20x baseline QPS for 60s using replay of production request mix (prefix-heavy chat + long token generations)
Enable proxy debug hooks and force connection churn by toggling keepalive at 15s intervals
Trigger KV compaction job on a staging shard with traffic to observe compaction full-scan path under load
Run SDK with default retry/backoff to observe amplification and added latency in backend traces
mitigation_summary: Immediate: Short-lived tenant-level egress shaping and temporary request-rate cap (10 req/s per-tenant) to stop retry storms (rollback key: remove tenant cap)
Immediate: Flip proxy keepalive heuristic to conservative mode to avoid slow-drain (config flag: proxy.keepalive.safe=true)
Hotfix: Patch KV compaction to use incremental windowed compaction instead of full shard scans (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1248)
Client guidance: Publish SDK advisory to add jitter to retry windows and to use idempotency keys for streaming endpoints (DOC: https://confluence.redwood.ai/SDK-retry-guidance)
Observability: Add new per-tenant active connection gauge and compaction-latency SLO alerts on Datadog dashboard (Dashboard: https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/hosted-api/tenant-connections)
Customer comms: Sent interim incident notes to impacted customers and bucketed them by severity for follow-ups (PagerDuty incident PD-8891)
tasks: Deploy proxy.keepalive.safe=true to edge-proxy fleet (canary -> region-wide) — owner: Network Team
Merge and deploy KV compaction patch (infra PR #1248) with feature flag off by default — owner: Storage Team
Roll out per-tenant rate limiter in front of model-router (small canary on non-critical tenants) — owner: Routing Team
Publish SDK advisory and include patched client sample in python/js SDKs — owner: SDK Team
Add tracing tags to correlate connection resets with compaction events — owner: Observability Team
Prepare postmortem and customer RCA doc for exec & CS — owner: Incident Lead
acceptance_criteria: No new tenant-facing 5xx waves for 72 hours post rollout under comparable burst tests
Per-tenant tail latency reduced to baseline +25% during simulated bursts
KV compaction runs without full-shard blocking and shows <100ms p99 compaction latency in staging
Customer SDK advisory and code samples published and referenced in customer comms
rollout_plan: Step 1 (T+0): Apply temporary tenant caps and enable proxy.safe keepalive across all edge proxies — monitor 30m
Step 2 (T+1h): Canary deploy KV compaction patch to a single storage shard cluster with feature-flag on; run burst replay
Step 3 (T+4h): If canary stable, enable compaction patch region-wide and start staged rollout of per-tenant rate limiter
Step 4 (T+24h): Remove temporary tenant caps once rate limiter demonstrates stability; continue 72h elevated monitoring
Rollback criteria: If p50 latency increases >50% for >10m or new 5xx regression observed, revert compaction flag and proxy config
monitoring_and_metrics: Dashboard: tenant-connections (active connections, connection resets, pool utilization)
Logs: correlate compaction job IDs with connection reset traces via trace.tag(compaction_id)
SRE runbook: run tenant-isolation playbook and escalate to on-call storage engineer
risks_and_open_questions: Risk: Rate limiting may impact latency-sensitive low-volume tenants — mitigated via tiered exceptions and manual override
Open: Need confirmation from Security if compaction flag touches any encrypted metadata paths (ticketed to Security: SEC-1172)
Open: Evaluate whether Dedicated tenants should get a stricter isolation policy vs Hosted tenants; coordinate with Sales/Account Managers
followups_and_postmortem_tasks: Complete full incident postmortem and timeline (link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/incidents/ENG-33456-pm)
Implement long-term KV eviction redesign to avoid blocking sweeps (design doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1KV-evict-redesign)
Integrate adaptive client-aware backpressure into model-router and expose knob to Dedicated customers
Add SDK-level idempotency enforcement patterns and test harness for streaming endpoints
